content: The WikiDoc Scholars program is committed to a transparent and objective evaluation process for assessing your performance as a participant. This document serves as a tool for self-assessment and provides a framework for understanding the expectations and requirements for obtaining a letter of recommendation. However, it is important to note that participation in the program does not guarantee matching into a residency program. Throughout the year, you are encouraged to print this document and highlight the metrics that best represent your contributions to WikiDoc. You have the autonomy to set your own performance trajectory, which can range from below average (D) to excellent (A). Your academic performance, both in quality and quantity, will play a significant role in defining your career trajectory. To qualify for a letter of recommendation, you must meet the following criteria: 1. Actively participate in the WikiDoc Scholars program for a minimum of three months. 2. Complete at least four microchapters or six single pages within the three-month period. The process for obtaining a letter of recommendation involves submitting a formal request and providing objective metrics of your performance in college, medical school, and the WikiDoc program. These metrics will be verified against your CV. Depending on your career path within WikiDoc, the letter should include specific accomplishments, such as the number of months you participated, the number of questions completed in the Board Review Project, or the number of topics completed in various projects (e.g., Dermatology Atlas, Drug Project, Genetic Disorder Project). The letter will also evaluate your competencies in several areas, including: Work Product: The quality and quantity of your contributions, ranging from poor (frequent errors and lack of attention to detail) to outstanding (less than 1% error rate and excellent accuracy). Dependability: Your reliability in fulfilling responsibilities, from poor (frequent absences and tardiness) to outstanding (always on time and consistently dependable). Cooperativeness: Your ability to work with others, from poor (negative attitude and lack of teamwork) to outstanding (a natural leader who inspires and uplifts the team). Adaptability: Your capacity to adjust to changes, from poor (requiring constant supervision) to outstanding (proactively seeking solutions and adapting to new systems). Communication: Your effectiveness in giving and receiving information, from poor (condescending tone and incomplete messages) to outstanding (emotionally intelligent and compelling communication skills). Daily Decision-Making/Problem-Solving: Your ability to think critically and solve problems, from poor (reactive and disorganized) to outstanding (creative, proactive, and sound judgment). Use of Equipment and Materials: Your care and efficiency in handling resources, from poor (damaging equipment) to outstanding (independently troubleshooting and solving technical issues). Leadership Skills: Your ability to lead, from poor (dictatorial and impatient) to outstanding (charismatic, empathetic, and visionary leadership). The letter will conclude with a summary statement reflecting your overall performance and potential. While a strong recommendation letter is valuable, it is not sufficient on its own to secure a residency position, as other factors such as board scores also play a critical role. The letter may include personalized statements about your suitability for residency or employment, and it will highlight your unique strengths and achievements. In summary, the WikiDoc Scholars program provides a structured framework for evaluating and documenting your contributions, with the ultimate goal of supporting your career aspirations. However, success in matching into a residency program will depend on a combination of factors, including your performance in the program and other academic metrics.
